_description: Math-focused node taxonomy for VFX artists building Unreal materials. Use this when the material problem is mostly about arithmetic, thresholds, oscillation, vector math, channel packing, or procedural remapping rather than only texture sampling.
overview: Most production VFX materials are built from math before they are built from art textures. These nodes shape masks, remap ranges, drive loops, control procedural timing, and transform vectors between spaces. A senior VFX workflow uses these nodes intentionally to reduce texture dependence, expose cleaner controls, and keep master materials more reusable.

categories.why_it_matters: These are the atomic math nodes behind almost every material graph.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Offset values, shift masks, or combine scalar and vector lanes.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Add and Subtract to move values first before adding more expensive shaping logic.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Scale intensity, scale vectors, or normalize against a divisor.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Multiply is one of the most common graph nodes in VFX. Treat Divide with more care and protect against invalid assumptions about the denominator.
most_important_nodes.warning: Dividing by zero or by unstable near-zero values can produce broken output or NaN-like behavior.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Apply exponential shaping to contrast or falloff curves.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Reach for Power when the curve shape itself matters, especially for emissive and alpha shaping.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Reduce a value with square-root response instead of linear or power growth.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use SquareRoot when the graph wants a softer contrast response than Power.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Invert a mask or normalized value with 1 - x.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Prefer OneMinus over rebuilding a manual invert chain.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Convert negative values to positive magnitude while preserving positive values.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Abs is useful when you care about magnitude but not direction sign.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Keep only the fractional portion of a value.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Frac is a core node for looping behavior and custom atlas logic.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Return the remainder after division.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Fmod is useful when the wrap interval matters explicitly rather than only the fractional part.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Quantize values upward, downward, or to the nearest integer.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Floor for stepped frame timing and custom flipbook logic. Use Round only when nearest-value quantization is the real intent.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Return sign classification: negative, zero, or positive.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Sign when the graph logic depends on direction polarity more than on the original value magnitude.

categories.why_it_matters: These nodes clamp, remap, threshold, and blend procedural values into artist-friendly control bands.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Limit a value to a chosen range.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Clamp when graph safety matters more than minimal instruction count.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Clamp to the 0-1 range efficiently.
typical_vfx_usage: cheap range safety for blend factors
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Prefer Saturate over Clamp when the intended range is exactly 0 to 1.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Keep the larger or smaller of two values.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Max and Min to combine control lanes without branching.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Blend between A and B using an alpha value.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Treat Lerp as one of the core composition nodes in VFX graph design.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Create hard or soft thresholds.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Step when the edge should be hard. Use SmoothStep when a procedural mask needs controlled softness.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Perform explicit branch-style conditional evaluation.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use If sparingly. In production VFX, math-based blends are often preferred over explicit branching for predictability and shader friendliness.

categories.why_it_matters: These nodes create cyclic motion, oscillation, angular math, and rotation-aware effects.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Generate periodic oscillation over time.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Sine or Cosine when rhythm matters and the motion should repeat continuously.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Produce a tangent response curve for sharper periodic behavior.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use Tangent cautiously because it can spike aggressively compared to Sine or Cosine.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Convert values into inverse trigonometric outputs.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Inverse trig is a specialist tool. Use it when the graph truly needs angular reconstruction or normalized directional analysis.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Compute an angle from a 2D directional vector with proper quadrant handling.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Atan2 is usually the best choice when a graph needs stable angle output from XY coordinates.

categories.why_it_matters: This is where material work shifts from simple scalar shaping into real directional and space-aware logic.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Measure directional similarity between two vectors.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Dot Product is a foundational directional test and should be second nature in VFX graph work.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Generate a perpendicular vector from two inputs.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Cross Product matters when the graph needs a real perpendicular direction rather than just a scalar similarity test.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Convert a vector to unit length while preserving direction.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Normalize when only direction matters and vector magnitude should not affect the downstream logic.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Compute vector magnitude or separation between two positions.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Distance and Length are core procedural tools for radial and proximity-based effects.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Compute the reflected view vector.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use ReflectionVector when the effect read depends on reflected viewing direction, not just surface angle.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Move vectors or positions between tangent, local, world, view, camera, or instance spaces.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: When the effect breaks because of coordinate space confusion, Transform or TransformPosition is often the missing correction.

categories.why_it_matters: Packed data workflows depend on extracting, reassembling, and routing channels cleanly.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Extract chosen channels from a vector or packed texture.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: Use ComponentMask aggressively in packed-texture workflows, but keep channel meaning documented.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Combine smaller values into a larger vector.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: AppendVector is usually the lowest-friction way to construct UVs or vector parameters from scalar lanes.

most_important_nodes.primary_role: Split or assemble vector components through reusable material functions.
most_important_nodes.agent_rule: These are helpful readability functions when a graph becomes too dense with masks and append chains.

categories.why_it_matters: Engine material functions provide reusable math blocks with clearer artist intent than rebuilding the same subgraph repeatedly.

most_important_functions.primary_role: Quickly increase or decrease contrast on a mask.
most_important_functions.agent_rule: Use CheapContrast when the graph only needs a fast contrast push rather than a custom power-shaped response.

most_important_functions.primary_role: Map a value from one numeric interval into another.
most_important_functions.agent_rule: Use RemapValueRange when the graph needs readable artist-facing remap logic instead of nested subtract/divide/multiply chains.

most_important_functions.primary_role: Convert a value into alpha based on its position between a start and end range.
most_important_functions.agent_rule: This is a strong helper for procedural gradients, distance ramps, and threshold pre-processing.

most_important_functions.primary_role: Convert UVs to polar-like radial coordinates.
most_important_functions.agent_rule: Use this for radial masks, shockwaves, circles, and angle-based flow rather than rebuilding the full polar conversion every time.

agent_guardrails: Prefer Saturate over Clamp when the intended output range is exactly 0 to 1.
Avoid explicit If branching unless the material logic truly requires it and a math blend cannot express the same result cleanly.
Use Floor and Frac together for custom flipbook logic, but prefer ParticleSubUV when the stock workflow already covers the need.
When a procedural graph becomes hard to read, consider a Material Function before escalating to a Custom HLSL node.
Coordinate-space bugs often look like UV bugs; verify whether Transform or TransformPosition is the missing step before changing the texture logic.

cross_reference_playbook.foundational_nodes: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/vfx_artist_essential_node_taxonomy.json for the simpler node families.
cross_reference_playbook.advanced_environment_work: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/vfx_artist_advanced_node_taxonomy.json for depth-aware, world-aware, and optimization-heavy shader authoring.
cross_reference_playbook.flipbook_work: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/particle_subuv_flipbook_fire_smoke.json when Floor, Frac, and atlas logic are being used around flipbook materials.
cross_reference_playbook.uv_motion: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/panning_uv.json when the material also depends on scrolling UV flow.
cross_reference_playbook.radial_effects: Pair with Knowledge/Materials/Techniques/portal_ring.json when VectorToRadialValue and threshold math are central to the effect.
